solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plan beach excursion as part of healthy regime

indicators.note: an excursion is a jaunt off the usual route, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A day trip to the seaside is recommended as part of a healthy lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excursion' is the anagram signal, rearranging PLANBEACH. pH is the chemist's scale of acidity, as in skin-care advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping the body's acidity level right is promoted as one element of a healthy regime.

clue.text: Thoroughfare going around north in rocky hill or volcano in the Andes

indicators.note: the word in places the road-and-north piece within the rocky hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

indicators.note: the thoroughfare goes round, enclosing the letter for north

parts.note: a road is a thoroughfare
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Directions for a road skirting northward through rocky high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop typical of Dartmoor; 'or' looks like a choice between hill and volcano but is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tronador is an extinct volcano on the border of Argentina and Chile, in the Andes range.

clue.text: Unique, unlike 'another place'

definitions.meaning: MPs call the House of Lords 'another place'; it is full of peers, so being unlike it means having none

explanation.surface: Describing something singular as quite different from somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons, members refer to the House of Lords as 'another place' rather than by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal has no peers, the second reading taking that word as Lords.

clue.text: Froth on liquor a third of pub staff removed

indicators.note: two letters from six is a third of the word for pub staff
taken away, so that third is dropped from the end

parts.note: a barman is a member of pub staff

explanation.surface: Foam on a drink after a third of the bar workers have been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third of' ... 'removed' drops AN, two of BARMAN's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Barm is the frothy yeast that forms on top of fermenting malt liquors such as beer.

clue.text: Composer making a connection between two notes a tone apart

indicators.note: the connection sits between the two notes, inside them

parts.note: G is a musical note
A is a musical note, one whole tone above G
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A composer bridging two pitches a whole step apart in his music.
explanation.walkthrough: G and A are a tone apart on the scale, so 'a tone apart' confirms which two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a Russian composer, often called the father of Russian classical music.

clue.text: Commodity past its best without smallest amount of preservatives

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside, so the stale piece wraps round

parts.note: stale food is past its best

indicators.note: just the first letter, the least that can be taken from the word

explanation.surface: Food goods going off because they contain hardly any preservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: P, the first letter of 'preservatives', goes inside STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a principal product or basic item of trade, such as grain.

clue.text: Suggest one politician's extremely lazy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: taking the word at its extremes, first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Hinting that a certain member of parliament is bone idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes L and Y, the ends of 'lazy'; the 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to hint at it indirectly, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Israel hot and bothered with Turkish standard

indicators.note: flustered and agitated, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Israel getting heated in a quarrel with Turkey over a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' rearranges ISRAELHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman Turks carried a horse's tail on a pole as a banner of rank, so it served as a standard.

clue.text: Spell "discharge" backwards

indicators.note: the synonym for discharge is read from end to start

parts.note: to emit is to discharge

explanation.surface: An instruction to write out a word in reverse letter order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like a verb about letters; it is the noun, a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a stretch or period, as in a spell of fine weather.

clue.text: Said to check the weather

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be looking at the forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' signals the sound: REIN and RAIN are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is a kind of weather, and in British speech the weather often simply means rainfall outdoors.

clue.text: A novel of the Eternal city

definitions.meaning: French for a novel, also used in English for a long prose story
belonging to Rome, called the Eternal City

explanation.surface: A book set in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman means relating to Rome, the Eternal City; a roman is also a novel, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Part of one's used to make a cross sometimes handed out in Papal Mass

definitions.text: Part of one's used to make a cross sometimes handed out

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: Something given out during a Mass led by the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of one's ... handed' hints at one's hand; on Palm Sunday churches hand out small crosses folded from palm leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is part of one's hand, and palm leaves are folded into crosses given out on Palm Sunday.

clue.text: Front of negligee laced wrongly — that's wicked!

indicators.note: laced up the wrong way, so the letters are put in a new order
only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A nightdress laced up badly, with an exclamation of naughty delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of' takes N from 'negligee'; 'wrongly' rearranges it with LACED. 'Wicked' means having a wick.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle has a wick, so it is literally the thing that is wicked.

clue.text: Former princess made to abandon crown

parts.note: Di, Diana, the late Princess of Wales

indicators.note: read as wild abandon, so the letters are thrown about freely

explanation.surface: A former royal forced to give up her crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandon' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in 'with abandon', rearranging MADE into ADEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled band worn on the head as a sign of royalty.

clue.text: Deserted Iran perhaps in Iraqi capital

indicators.note: perhaps hints the country's name is only a possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A war-torn, abandoned Iran pictured beside the city of Baghdad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means money, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is Iraq's unit of currency, and capital here means money.

clue.text: Missions to find fish that is seen in German river

indicators.note: these pieces appear inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ems flows through north-west Germany
a bass is a fish
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Expeditions sent to locate fish in a German river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missions' sounds like errands or quests; it is the diplomatic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Embassies are diplomatic missions, an ambassador's staff sent to a foreign country.

clue.text: Chat with Henry's mum about plant

indicators.note: the letters are moved round about into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here
taken as written, at the end of the answer

explanation.surface: Having a chat with Henry's mother about gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHAT and HENRYS; 'mum', left in place, is also a nickname for this flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a flowering garden plant, often shortened to mum.

clue.text: One enjoying pursuit with bicycle getting gold medal place

parts.note: a hobby, short for hobby-horse, was an early pedal-less bicycle
1st place wins gold, written here as I and ST

explanation.surface: A cyclist who enjoys riding and comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST is read with the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist is someone who pursues an activity for pleasure in their spare time.

clue.text: English translation of French novel somehow bringing Stan fame

indicators.note: by some unknown means, so the letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A translator named Stan gains renown from putting a French book into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges STANFAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Malraux's La Condition humaine was published in English under this title, so it is the English version.

clue.text: Web designer beginning to swallow pride perhaps

indicators.note: just the start, the first letter of the bird's name
perhaps suggests the word is one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A website creator having to eat humble pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web designer' suggests the internet, and 'swallow pride' a phrase; 'perhaps' rearranges the second word into PIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins and designs its own web, so it is a designer of webs in nature.

clue.text: Promise to turn record over on side

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the record sits on top of the side
turning the record round reverses its letters

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
an edge is a side

explanation.surface: A vow to flip a vinyl record onto its other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses LP; 'over' then stacks it above EDGE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise, so the two words share a meaning.

clue.text: Show a large-scale work in Design and Technology

indicators.note: the word places the work inside the school subject's abbreviation

parts.note: DT is the British school subject Design and Technology
an epic is a large-scale work such as a long film or poem

explanation.surface: Presenting a major project in a school design class.
explanation.walkthrough: DT, Design and Technology, is a subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to show or portray something in a picture or words.

clue.text: Boy and girl in former Indian province

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young couple living in an old region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal was a province of British India, later split between India and present-day Bangladesh.

clue.text: Black and blue Roman numerals

definitions.meaning: bruised, the purplish colour of a bruise
the letters read as numbers 50, 4, 1 and 500 in Roman style

explanation.surface: Bruised colouring and old Latin number symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters split as L, IV, I, D, each a valid Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid originally means the dark bluish-grey colour of bruised skin.

clue.text: That's awful about minister finally getting sack

indicators.note: the exclamation goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust or disapproval

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Outrage at a government minister finally being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R, the end of 'minister', and 'about' puts FIE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them from their job, the same as to fire them.

clue.text: £25 found outside energy plant

indicators.note: the sum of money sits outside, around the energy symbol

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Twenty-five pounds turning up outside a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a power plant in this picture; it is the flower. A pony is British slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: The peony is a garden plant grown for its large showy flowers.

clue.text: Steer close to English county shortly

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
on can mean near, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: Guiding cattle near a county of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb; it is the animal. Oxon is the short form of Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxon is the standard abbreviation for Oxfordshire, so it is the county named in short.

clue.text: Weatherman's angle

definitions.meaning: Michael ..., a long-serving BBC television weather forecaster
to angle is to try to catch with rod and line

explanation.surface: A forecaster's particular slant on things.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Fish was a famous BBC TV weather presenter; the 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling is the sport of catching with a rod, so to angle is a verb for the same pastime.

clue.text: Buzz Aldrin generally contributes

indicators.note: the two words each supply some of the letters, running across the gap

explanation.surface: Astronaut Buzz Aldrin usually chips in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' looks like Aldrin's first name; it is the definition, as in 'give me a buzz'.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is an informal word for a phone call, as is a ring.

clue.text: Architectural feature of very large place included in credit note

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the credit note pair

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
to set is to place

explanation.surface: Part of a building describing an outsize location noted on a credit slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit note' looks like one thing but splits in two; OS (outsize) is the clothing label for very large.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossette is a projecting ear at the corner of a door or window frame in classical building design.
